newsitem.title: UK: Russia shines in sporadic London LDC trade.
newsitem.headline: Russia shines in sporadic London LDC trade.

text.p: Russia shone once again in a thin emerging debt market that saw sporadic buying across the board ahead of non-farm payroll data due shortly in the United States.

"Russia's up because it's cheap," said one trader, who saw nothing but ongoing anticipation over Russia's forthcoming debt rating and its subsequent dollar Eurobond issue to explain the market's firmness.
"It looks like a case of people buying the rumour and selling the fact," he said. "People are still buying the rumour."
Earlier this week talk that Russia would receive a rating possibly as high as BB+ drove the market upwards, but one trader said BB- looked more likely.
"But prices are reflecting a straight double B," he said. "Dollar Vnesh and Principals are quite strong."
He quoted Russia Prins up about one point at 54-00, and dollar Vnesh loans up about 1/2 point at 74-3/8.

One dealer said Russian debt was flavour of the month among U.S. investors. "The U.S. loves Russia, they just can't get enough," he said, adding the Eurobond will have novelty value that will overshadow any political uncertainty there.
Traders reported spots of buying in Mexican, Venezuelan and Brazilian instruments, but said volumes were small.
"There's been scattered buying across the board -- it's a typical Friday morning," said one at a major European firm.
But he added that the pockets of interest may have come from dealers expecting the market to trade up after key U.S. September payroll data this afternoon.
Traders are mainly confident that the numbers will come in low enough to dispel doubts about the Federal Reserve's steady monetary policy.

Bulgarian paper gained slightly during the morning after opening weak. Dealers are still holding out for word on its delayed IMF loan tranche, with an announcement from the Fund possible within the next few weeks.
Among Latin paper, Argentine FRBs strengthened slightly, rising 1/8 to a screen price of 59-5/8. Brazilian C bonds were flat at 71-1/4, and Mexican Discs rose 1/8 to 84-5/8.
